Hi Sam — appreciate the specificity. Quick technical rundown and an example timeline below. I’ll include the exceptions and audit evidence points so your team can map them to the questionnaire.

Key definitions / scope:
- "Customer production data": requests, prompt text, documents, attachments submitted via Redwood API or uploaded to a customer-dedicated instance.
- "Operational artifacts": structured logs (ingestion logs, routing metadata), aggregated telemetry, ephemeral KV cache entries, and debug snapshots created when a request triggers an error.
- "Training usage": any inclusion of customer data into datasets used to update model weights or fine-tune models intended for future inference.

Assurance:
- Redwood policy: customer production data is excluded from training datasets used for model updates. We maintain controls to prevent automatic ingestion of customer payloads into training pipelines.
- Operational artifacts: we do not include operational artifacts in training datasets either, but some artifacts are short-lived and exist for debugging and performance operational needs before deletion.

Example deletion sequence (ordered steps, approximate timings):
1) Tombstone flag set immediately (within seconds) when a deletion API request is accepted — request remains addressable to ops for <24h for verification and rollback windows.
2) Live eviction job runs within 24–72 hours to remove data from active nodes, KV caches, and prefix caches.
3) Additional ephemeral snapshots (used for debugging) marked for deletion; background jobs scrub these within 7–14 days depending on retention policy for the environment.
4) Backups / snapshots used for disaster recovery are retained per our backup retention policy; deletion propagation to long-term backups occurs on the next scheduled backup lifecycle event and can be up to 90 days in worst-case (but for customer-specific tombstones we record a deletion marker that prevents restore of that dataset).
5) Final verification and tombstone audit record generated and stored in audit logstore (immutable) — the audit log contains the deletion event, actor, and job IDs.

Notes and caveats:
- Embeddings or derived artifacts: embeddings computed on customer requests are treated as derivative customer artifacts and are deleted according to the same sequence unless a customer has opted into analytics that explicitly stores derivatives.
- Reproducibility / legal holds: if FinCo places a legal hold, we suspend the deletion sequence and record the hold.
- Snapshots used for debugging: some debug snapshots may be redacted rather than fully removed immediately if they are needed for ongoing incident investigations. Redaction records are kept.

Audit evidence we can produce:
- Signed one-page attestation (PDF).
- Deletion job logs and job IDs for a sample deletion request (we can provide sanitized logs and hashes).
- Diagram of deletion propagation (PNG).

I’ll attach a draft attestation and diagram for your review. If you need a shorter technical appendix that maps our controls to SOC 2 criteria (CC6, CC7 etc.), we can add that as well.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Privacy Operations — Redwood Inference
